page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-48-lssd is an ARM-based server instance powered by the c4a family. It features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 3.0 GHz. The processor operates with one thread per core, meaning hyperthreading is not active. It is equipped with 384 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of 4020 GB of NVMe SSD capacity.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance falls into the top 25% tier with a score of 86659.83, while single-core performance is in the middle 50% at 1821.19. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 5935.14 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and maintaining 334.84 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads, alongside 158.43 GB/sec for large-block writes. Data processing benchmarks show strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 532.16 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression at 32.3 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the combination of high-density ARM cores, a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and integrated local NVMe SSDs offers a resource-dense profile for memory-bound and I/O-intensive workloads without the overhead of x86 licensing. The lack of GPU acceleration and specialized AVX or AMX instruction sets represents a tradeoff for machine learning training, but the high memory capacity and fast local storage make it suitable for large-scale databases, memory-intensive data processing, and multi-threaded enterprise applications.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-48-lssd is an ARM64 server instance featuring 48 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 3.0 GHz. It is equipped with 384 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per core ratio, and includes 4020 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results place its multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth in the top 25% tier, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 334.84 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 532.16 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core CPU performance sits in the middle 50% tier. Lacking GPU hardware and x86-specific vector extensions, this instance offers a resource-dense, qualitatively cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. It is highly suitable for large-scale databases, multi-threaded data processing, and memory-optimized enterprise applications.
